findings.issue: No test script, no test runner in devDependencies, zero test files in the app; the acceptance suite is the only guard on a codebase with substantial data-transformation logic.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (already Vite-based) with unit tests for the pure helpers in lib/format.ts, lib/home-url.ts and lib/data.ts, plus a Playwright smoke test for the pagination/sort interactions.

findings.issue: Pagination (slice bounds, parseInt fallback, min/max clamping) and default-omitting URL building in home-url.ts are untested; off-by-one and clamp regressions would render empty or wrong pages.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test homeUrl() against the omit-defaults rule and extract the page-clamp math into a tested pure function (e.g. paginate(matches, page, 48)).

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion (id < 10000), dedup and dex-number sort in pokemonRefsToSpecies are all one-line-regression territory with visible consequences on move/ability/type lists.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test pokemonRefsToSpecies with fixture refs containing a Mega (>10000), a duplicate, and deoxys-normal→deoxys, asserting the species link and ordering.

findings.issue: The MAX_CONCURRENT semaphore's release path (queue.shift() in finally) and the cache's LRU/TTL bookkeeping are untested; a missed release would deadlock every request and no test would fail.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that pushes >MAX_CONCURRENT concurrent api() calls against a stubbed fetch and asserts all resolve; also test 404→null and error→cache-eviction behavior.

findings.issue: Missing-values-sort-last in both directions and the aria-sort toggle are untested; the standard refactor of applying `sign` to the blank comparison silently breaks descending sort.
findings.suggestion: Playwright test: click a header with null Power/Accuracy values twice and assert blanks stay last and aria-sort flips.

findings.issue: Silent fallback for an invalid ?game=, the dedup key for learned moves, and the highest-order default game are untested; any of these regressing changes which moves render with no failure.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the game selection and table-grouping logic by extracting it from the route handler into a pure function over fixture API payloads.

findings.issue: The AbortController-based result swap prevents stale responses overwriting newer ones; deleting it during simplification introduces a race only visible on slow networks.
findings.suggestion: Playwright test typing two search queries quickly and asserting the rendered list matches the final query.

findings.issue: Pure, dependency-free helpers covering spec-defined edge cases (humanize, dexNumber padding, last-English flavor text, orDash) are the cheapest possible coverage and are untested.
findings.suggestion: A ten-line vitest file covering each helper's spec examples (mr-mime → Mr Mime, 25 → #0025) would pin the display rules.

findings.issue: The 404→null contract underpins every route's not-found path; if load() threw on 404 instead, all bad slugs would become 500s.
findings.suggestion: Include a 404 case in the api.ts unit tests.

findings.issue: The gracile-static hostname guard is what keeps API data out of the build; removing it reintroduces build-time data fetching, the exact violation the live-overlay acceptance test targets.
findings.suggestion: A unit test asserting isBuildRender() truthiness for a synthetic build URL documents the invariant.

summary: The agent wrote no tests at all — no runner, no script, no dev dependency — leaving the acceptance suite as the sole guard over genuinely risky logic: pagination/clamping, alternate-form filtering, a hand-rolled cache and concurrency semaphore, and client-side sorting with direction-dependent missing-value handling. The code is well factored for testing (pure helpers in lib/, data-returning route handlers), so the omission is cheap to fix: a vitest file over lib/ plus two Playwright interaction tests would cover the highest-risk paths. Until then, any refactor of the data layer or the filter/sort logic is flying blind.
